intro: This week’s intelligence digest highlights critical shifts at the intersection of retail, luxury, and AI, from evolving AML challenges in payments to innovative store concepts reshaping customer engagement. readOneThing.title: Payments, Fraud and AI: Why Retailers Can’t Afford to Ignore AML in 2026

items.title: Payments, Fraud and AI: Why Retailers Can’t Afford to Ignore AML in 2026
bullets: In 2026, online retailers face increased risks from diverse payment options including bank transfers, e-wallets, BNPL, and cryptocurrency, which criminals exploit for fraud and money laundering.
In 2024, money laundering accounted for £337 million of economic crime in the UK, with retail comprising 49% of fraud by value that year.
By 2025, 98% of merchants worldwide experienced fraud, with AI-driven schemes rapidly growing and prompting adoption of machine learning and biometric tools for real-time fraud detection.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: The article highlights that in 2026, online retailers must adapt to evolving customer payment preferences, including bank transfers, e-wallets, BNPL, and cryptocurrencies, emphasizing the importance of addressing anti-money laundering (AML) measures.

items.title: Dior Builds a Dream Store. Kohl’s Builds a Deal Rack. Both Have a Lesson for Jewelers.
bullets: Dior opened the Bamboo Pavilion in Tokyo's Daikanyama district, a 19,375-square-foot store blending French heritage with Japanese craftsmanship and luxury experience.
Kohl's introduced the Deal Bar across nearly all its 1,100 stores, featuring front-entrance displays with gifts and essentials priced under $10.
Federal Realty Investment Trust is investing up to $411 million in four residential-over-retail projects to increase foot traffic and strengthen retailer performance.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: The article from Instore Magazine (2026-03-06) discusses contrasting retail strategies by Dior and Kohl’s and explores their implications for the jewellery industry, including insights on how the "barbell economy" will affect customers in 2026.

items.title: Oracle and OpenAI drop Texas data centre expansion plan: Bloomberg
bullets: Oracle and OpenAI have abandoned plans to expand their AI data centre in Abilene, Texas, due to financing issues and OpenAI's changing needs. The proposed expansion included an additional 600 megawatts near the Stargate site, which will now be fulfilled at other campuses. The Stargate initiative, announced in January 2025, is a $500 billion project involving SoftBank, OpenAI, and Oracle to develop up to 10 gigawatts of data centre capacity.

items.title: Sportswear Brand On Sees Possible Boost From Lower US Tariff Rate
bullets: On Holding CEO Martin Hoffmann anticipates a potential sales boost following the Supreme Court's decision to strike down emergency US tariff levies. On forecasted at least 23 percent annual sales growth on a constant-currency basis for 2024, moderating from 30 percent in 2025, with a gross margin expected to rise to at least 63 percent. The US is On's largest market, where a temporary 10 percent tariff was imposed last week, planned to increase to 15 percent, which is lower than the previous 20 percent duty on imports from Vietnam and Indonesia.

items.title: Best Buy online marketplace gains traction as new profit driver
bullets: Best Buy's U.S. online marketplace generated approximately $300 million in gross merchandise value during fiscal Q4 2026, featuring over 1,100 third-party sellers.
More than 90% of marketplace sellers with active storefronts reported weekly sales, and over 80% of product returns were handled through physical stores.
The marketplace business is expected to move beyond its investment phase in fiscal 2027, contributing more significantly to operating income in fiscal 2028 and 2029.
items.summary: AI-generated summary: Best Buy's online marketplace is becoming a significant profit contributor, generating approximately $300 million in gross merchandise value during fiscal Q4 2026, providing the retailer with a new revenue stream amid uneven core sales.

items.title: For OpenAI and Anthropic, the competition is deeply personal
bullets: Anthropic, led by former OpenAI researcher Dario Amodei, is rapidly gaining enterprise customers and challenging OpenAI's dominance in the AI industry. The startup has more than doubled its projected revenue for this year to $19 billion, up from $9 billion last year. Both companies are headquartered in San Francisco and represent key competitors in the global AI race, with their rivalry intensifying over the past few months.

items.title: ‘Does Anyone Really Want a Birthday Card From Their Jeweler?’
bullets: Independent jewelry store owners are divided on the value of birthday outreach, with some sending gift cards and others abandoning the practice due to logistical challenges.
One jeweler reported sending a $1,000 gift card to a big spender who typically spends between $8,000 and $12,000 during visits.
